justification: Critical: the legislation monitor is the only detector of law changes; it reported 'all current' from 2026-06-08 while 24 of 33 registered instruments changed (measured live on the Fly server 2026-10-08). Every currency claim and stale notice depends on it.

pre_impl.existing_data: instrument_registry: 33 active rows; last change ever detected 2026-06-08; 7 instruments measured stale from this machine, 24 by the fixed monitor from the whitelisted Fly IP.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: PCO's export now returns records with keys title/view/xml/images only; the parser read URL, so every instrument_id was blank, and the 'Point In Time' custom query returns [] for any window. The monitor treated a PCO absence as 'confirmed unchanged' and stamped last_checked.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses check_via_nsw_legislation and _extract_latest_pit_date (already in the file, previously only behind --source nsw_legislation). Removes get_changes_since (only caller was the removed PCO version path).
pre_impl.external_source_error: A law page that cannot be read (HTTP error, download, no date, no URL) is a named fetch error; the run exits 1 and Telegram reports ERROR. All pages failing exits 1 immediately. PCO export empty/unreadable/denied is a named cross-check error.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend change. Output is the monitor's stdout summary, Telegram messages and instrument_registry writes.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: The operator sees 'Legislation Monitor ERROR' naming each law that could not be read; 'no changes' is sent only when every law's page was read and none moved.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any silent pass returns: five mutations (missing URL skipped, empty PCO export treated as no changes, unreadable PCO format accepted, PCO absence stamped as checked, PCO failure swallowed) each made 2-3 tests fail.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Observed 2026-10-08: each of the five mutations produced 2-3 failures out of 41; restored code 41 passed. Live: old code on Fly printed 'PCO: 0 instruments changed in last 35 days'; fixed code dry-run on Fly: Checked 33, Changed 24, Fetch errors 0.

functions.name: pco_listed_keys
functions.input: active instrument_registry rows with their pco_instrument_id values for the weekly export lookup
functions.output: the set of our instrument keys that PCO's weekly export lists as updated this week
functions.if_none: An empty export or unrecognised format raises; main() records it as a named cross-check error.

functions.name: pco_cross_check
functions.input: PCO-listed keys, the page-read version map, and the stored registry versions for each instrument
functions.output: one named error per instrument PCO lists as amended whose own page date did not move
functions.if_none: A page reading of None produces no cross-check error because that miss is already reported as a fetch error.

functions.name: _parse_changes
functions.input: PCO export JSON records in either the old URL format or the new view/xml format
functions.output: PCOChange objects with instrument_id taken from URL, view or xml paths of each record
functions.if_none: Records that yield no instrument ID at all raise PCOError instead of returning blank matches.

values.value: No new regulatory values; versions come from each law's legislation.nsw.gov.au page at run time
values.source: legislation.nsw.gov.au point-in-time links via the existing _extract_latest_pit_date
values.read_at: run time, once per instrument per weekly run on the Fly server
values.if_missing: A missing or unreadable date is a named fetch error and the run exits 1; nothing is stamped.

queries.where_clause: WHERE instrument_key = %s, only when a page reading exists (unchanged SQL)

break_it.scenario: PCO changes its export format again and every record parses with a blank instrument ID
break_it.what_happens: The parser raises PCOError and main records a named cross-check failure, exiting 1 instead of reporting no changes

break_it.scenario: PCO's weekly export comes back as an empty list during a normal week of NSW amendments
break_it.what_happens: pco_listed_keys raises and the run exits 1 with 'PCO export cross-check failed' rather than claiming all current

break_it.scenario: A law's own page returns HTTP 403, a download, no date, or the instrument has no legislation URL
break_it.what_happens: That law is a named fetch error, it is never stamped as checked, and the run exits 1 with an ERROR message
break_it.how: check_via_nsw_legislation errors plus no stamping on a miss
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_legislation_monitor_no_silent_pass.py tests/test_sepp_auto_stale.py -q -o addopts= -k 'url or 403 or download or partial'

break_it.scenario: A future edit restores the old rule that absence from PCO's export means confirmed unchanged
break_it.what_happens: check_instrument stamps last_checked on a miss and the registry goes stale silently again
break_it.how: tests assert no SQL on a miss for every source

break_it.scenario: The deployed Fly copy of the monitor drifts from the repo copy again
break_it.what_happens: The server would run old code while the repo looks fixed, as happened with a 129-line difference before this change
break_it.how: byte-equality test for the three deployed files

break_it.scenario: The load-active-instruments query returns rows whose page cannot be fetched at all from the Fly IP
break_it.what_happens: Every instrument fails, the run exits 1 immediately with an ERROR telegram listing the failures

break_it.scenario: The record-a-new-version query runs for an instrument with no page reading this week
break_it.what_happens: It cannot: check_instrument returns before any SQL when the reading is None, so no version or last_checked is written

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: fly deploy of deploy/flyio-legislation-monitor after merge; then the next weekly run writes the 24 changed versions and marks dependent standards stale (production write, separate go-ahead).
